# Adjudication Task — Chapter 193

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃193화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|열화문의 신물.
  6|
  7|화왕의 입에서 그 낯선 단어가 튀어나온 순간, 노호검객의 눈이 찢어질 듯 팽창했다.
  8|
  9|“그, 그게 무슨 말씀이십니까.”
 10|
 11|“칠순도 안 된 놈이 벌써부터 귓구멍이 막혔나. 한 번 더 말해 줄 테니 똑똑히 들어라.”
 12|
 13|적천강이 짜증 난 듯한 얼굴로 나를 향해 턱짓했다.
 14|
 15|“본문의 신물을 저놈한테 맡겼다. 됐느냐?”
 16|
 17|“…….”
 18|
 19|“…….”
 20|
 21|되긴 뭐가 돼.
 22|
 23|나는 황당한 얼굴로 주위를 둘러봤다. 진위경과 백무성을 포함한 모두가 경악한 얼굴로 나와 적천강을 번갈아 보는 중이었다.
 24|
 25|이 혼돈의 도가니 속, 유일하게 영향을 받지 않은 한 사람이 입을 열었다.
 26|
 27|“은인, 열화문의 신물이 뭐예요? 나도 보여 줘요.”
 28|
 29|나는 청풍의 질문에 대답할 수 없었다.
 30|
 31|‘나도 몰라, 이 새끼야.’
 32|
 33|열화문의 신물이라니. 뭐야 그게.
 34|
 35|맹세컨대 그런 물건은 듣도 보도 못했다.
 36|
 37|내가 적천강에게 받은 물건이라고는 화염신장의 비급과 검 한 자루뿐인……데.
 38|
 39|아, 잠깐만.
 40|
 41|“혹시?”
 42|
 43|설마 하는 내 시선에 적천강이 혀를 찼다.
 44|
 45|“등에 메어 놓고도 모르다니. 멍청한 놈.”
 46|
 47|망치로 뒤통수를 얻어맞은 기분이다.
 48|
 49|나는 황급히 단단히 고정시킨 매듭을 풀었다. 칭칭 감싸 둔 천을 벗겨 내자 낡고 투박한 검갑이 모습을 드러낸다.
 50|
 51|‘이름 없는 검.’
 52|
 53|조필이 스승에게서 훔치고, 나에게 빼앗긴 바로 그 물건.
 54|
 55|검파를 움켜쥐고 당겼다.
 56|
 57|스르릉, 솜털이 곤두서는 소리와 함께 새하얀 검신이 드러난다.
 58|
 59|내리깔린 어둠 속, 마치 전설 속 성검(聖劍)처럼 빛나는 모습에 사람들이 탄성을 내질렀다.
 60|
 61|‘그럼 이게 정말…… 열화문의 신물?’
 62|
 63|지금까지 단 한 번도 의심해 보지 않았다.
 64|
 65|왜 조필이 적천강에게서 이것을 훔쳤는지. 왜 화염신장이나 열화신단과 달리 [이름 없는 검]이라는 괴상한 설명이 붙었는지.
 66|
 67|내가 넋 나간 얼굴로 검신을 바라보던 그때였다.
 68|
 69|“이, 이건 말도 안 됩니다!”
 70|
 71|노호검객이다. 극도의 당황과 흥분에 휩싸인 그와는 달리 적천강의 안색은 평온, 그 자체였다.
 72|
 73|“무엇이 말이냐?”
 74|
 75|“그, 그것이.”
 76|
 77|“노부가 저 녀석에게 열화문의 신물을 맡겼다. 네놈이 제아무리 대가리에 똥만 가득 찬 놈이라지만 그것이 무슨 뜻인지 모르지 않을 터.”
 78|
 79|순간 정신이 번쩍 들었다.
 80|
 81|검에 정신이 팔려서 잠시 잊고 있었다. 한 문파, 그것도 수백 년간 일인전승으로 계승된 열화문의 신물이 가진 의미를.
 82|
 83|더불어 불과 반나절 전에 청풍이 했던 말이 뇌리를 스쳤다.
 84|
 85|
 86|
 87|‘은인을 제자로 삼으려는 것 아니에요?’
 88|
 89|
 90|
 91|당시에는 허무맹랑한 헛소리라 생각하고 웃어넘겼다.
 92|
 93|하지만 이제는…….
 94|
 95|‘시바, 나도 모르겠다.’
 96|
 97|마른침만 꼴깍거리는 내게 노호검객의 삿대질이 날아들었다.
 98|
 99|하지만 미처 입을 떼기도 전에 적천강의 무시무시한 눈빛이 그를 꽁꽁 옭아맸다.
100|
101|“노부가, 본문의 신물을, 맡겼다고 했다.”
102|
103|그것이 전부였다. 하지만 상대는 다름 아닌 화왕이다.
104|
105|노호검객에게는 반박할 수 있는 용기가 남아 있지 않았다. 입술을 잘근잘근 씹던 그가 돌연 나를 노려보았다.
106|
107|“놈. 운이 좋구나.”
108|
109|이 노인네는 왜 또 나한테 지랄이야.
110|
111|적천강도 별말이 없다. 이 정도는 알아서 해결하라는 건가? 나는 노호검객을 향해 어깨를 으쓱해 보였다.
112|
113|“사람 잘못 보셨네요. 저 운 되게 없는데.”
114|
115|내가 시발, 운이 좋았으면 너 같은 새끼를 만났겠냐.
116|
117|일촉즉발로 치닫던 상황에 적천강이 왔으니 이걸 대흉(大凶)이라고 해야 할지, 대길(大吉)이라고 해야 할지는 모르겠지만.
118|
119|“뭐 아무튼 만나서 반가웠습니다. 조심히 들어가시고요.”
120|
121|“교활한 놈. 어디 아까 전처럼 해 보지 그러느냐?”
122|
123|“아까 전처럼? 아, 좆 같다고 한 거요?”
124|
125|노호검객이 뭐라 할 틈도 없이 고개를 꾸벅 숙였다.
126|
127|“그 부분에 있어서는 죄송합니다. 제가 불의를 보면 못 참는 성격이라서. 까마득한 후배의 말실수라고 생각하고 봐주십쇼. 대. 협.”
128|
129|“……!”
130|
131|노호검객의 몸이 부르르 떨렸다. 꽉 움켜쥔 주먹에서는 피가 뚝뚝 떨어졌다.
132|
133|그의 모습에서 불과 몇 분 전의 내가 보였다. 우리 두 사람의 차이가 있다면 나는 노호검객에게 굴하지 않았지만 그는 화왕에게 굴복했다는 것이다.
134|
135|힘을 앞세운 자는 더 큰 힘 앞에 무릎을 꿇는다. 세상의 본질을 재확인한 것 같아 마냥 통쾌하지만은 않았다.
136|
137|아니, 오히려 씁쓸하기까지 했다.
138|
139|‘기분 더럽네.’
140|
141|적천강이 아니었다면 지금 저자가 느끼는 치욕과 분노는 나와 태원진가의 몫이 되었을 테니까.
142|
143|이 자리의 몇 사람만 나선다면 노호검객 개인을 쓰러트리는 건 어렵지 않다. 그러나 그의 뒤에는 종남파가 있다.
144|
145|인정하기는 싫지만…… 그들과 우리의 격차는 크다. 그것은 지금으로서는 결코 좁힐 수 없는 간격이다.
146|
147|‘지금은, 말이지.’
148|
149|만년 F급 헌터였던 내가 여기까지 왔다. 세상일은 어떻게 될지 모른다.
150|
151|혹시 모르지, 언젠가 태원진가가 구파일방, 오대세가와 어깨를 나란히 하게 될지도.
152|
153|‘아, 이건 너무 나갔나?’
154|
155|시골 면장이 대통령 선거에 도전하는 거나 마찬가지다.
156|
157|그런 생각을 하며 피식 웃자 노호검객이 이를 갈았다.
158|
159|“감히 나를 비웃어?”
160|
161|“원래 웃는 인상이라 그런 건데요.”
162|
163|“그 입 닥치지 못할까!”
164|
165|분노에 가득 찬 고함이 터져 나온 그 순간, 적천강의 오른발이 번개 같은 속도로 노호검객의 정강이를 걷어찼다.
166|
167|무려 초절정 고수의 조인트 킥이다.
168|
169|퍽!
170|
171|“커흑!”
172|
173|“너나 닥쳐라. 어린노무 새끼가 어디 어른 앞에서 목소리를 높여?”
174|
175|“지금 이게 무슨 짓입니까!”
176|
177|“이 새끼 보게. 가급적 좋게 끝내려고 했더니 매를 벌어?”
178|
179|뻑!
180|
181|“억!”
182|
183|와, 이건 제대로 들어갔다.
184|
185|방금 전보다 더 둔탁한 타격음과 함께 노호검객이 정강이를 붙잡고 쓰러졌다.
186|
187|‘크, 대종남파의 장로도 별수 없구나.’
188|
189|높은 사회적 위치에 환갑이 넘은 나이지만 상대가 워낙 넘사벽이었다.
190|
191|나이, 무공, 신분. 그 어느 것으로도 따라잡을 수 없는 존재가 바로 화왕 적천강 아닌가.
192|
193|“지랄도 그 정도면 병이니라. 할 만큼 했으면 이만 썩 꺼져라.”
194|
195|“……그러지요.”
196|
197|원독에 찬 눈빛으로 나를 노려본 노호검객이 흙투성이가 된 몸을 일으키던 그때, 서늘한 목소리가 이어졌다.
198|
199|“또한 내 오늘 일은 불문에 부칠 터이니 다시는 이에 관해 논하지 말거라. 무슨 말인지 알아들었느냐?”
200|
201|이거 정말 팬클럽이라도 만들어야겠다.
202|
203|일단 내킨 걸음이라 막 지르긴 했지만 내심 걱정이 있었던 것도 사실이다. 후일 노호검객이 종남파를 앞세워 보복한다면 태원진가로서는 막을 방법이 없기 때문이다.
204|
205|하지만 적천강의 중재가 있다면 말이 달라진다.
206|
207|‘중재인지 협박인지는 모르겠지만.’
208|
209|오늘 일에 대한 앙금은 남겠지만 최소한 공식적인 압박을 가해 오지는 않을 것이다.
210|
211|설령 그런 일이 있더라도 화왕이라는 든든한 방파제가 있으니 부담감이 훨씬 적다.
212|
213|“왜 대답이 없느냐?”
214|
215|개수작을 간파당한 노호검객의 얼굴은 참혹하게 일그러져 있었다. 물론 적천강은 아랑곳하지 않았다.
216|
217|“네 입으로 말해라. 지금 당장.”
218|
219|“……알겠습니다. 제 이름을 걸고 약속하지요.”
220|
221|“네깟놈 주제에 무슨 이름을 걸어? 종남파의 이름으로 약속해라.”
222|
223|“으드득, 알겠습니다.”
224|
225|그제야 적천강의 입가에 흡족한 미소가 떠올랐다. 그가 허허 웃으며 노호검객의 어깨를 두드렸다.
226|
227|“어린노무 새끼가 어디서 이빨 가는 법을 배웠누. 확 그냥 이빨을 죄다 잡아 뽑아 버릴까 보다.”
228|
229|“…….”
230|
231|“허허허, 노부도 나이가 있으니 사람들 보는 앞에서 그럴 수도 없고. 껄껄껄!”
232|
233|호호백발 노인의 웃음이 이렇게 무서울 수 있다는 걸 처음 알았다.
234|
235|노호검객뿐만 아니라 듣고 있던 사람들 모두가 동시에 몸을 움찔 떨 정도다.
236|
237|악귀처럼 웃던 적천강이 내게 고개를 돌렸다.
238|
239|“네 녀석도 잘한 것 없다. 사정이 어찌 되었건 까마득한 어른에게 그런 폭언을 퍼붓다니. 제정신이냐?”
240|
241|나는 냉큼 고개를 숙였다. 어찌 되었건 사실은 사실이고, 종남파의 장로인 노호검객과 이쯤에서 마무리를 지어야겠다는 생각이 들었기 때문이다.
242|
243|“죄송합니다.”
244|
245|“아무리 나이를 똥구멍으로 처먹었어도 환갑이면 너만 한 손주가 있어도 이상하지 않을 나이다.”
246|
247|“……아, 네.”
248|
249|“아무리 개 같은 놈이어도 어른이고 무림의 대선배다. 더럽고 치사해도 앞으로는 예의를 깍듯이 갖추어라.”
250|
251|“송 대협. 진심으로 사죄드리겠습니다.”
252|
253|폴더 인사를 하고 허리를 펴자 붉게 달아오른 노호검객의 얼굴이 보인다. 사과를 받아도 받은 기분이 아닐 거다.
254|
255|반면 나는 싫은 놈에게 사과를 하고도 운기조식을 한 것처럼 기분이 상쾌했다.
256|
257|‘이게 바로 연륜인가.’
258|
259|백 년의 세월 동안 단련된 말빨 봐라.
260|
261|무공만 초절정이 아니다. 이 정도면 별호를 화왕이 아니라 혀왕으로 바꿔도 될 정도다.
262|
263|자신의 입회하에 모든 합의 절차를 끝마친 혀왕은 준엄한 목소리로 선언했다.
264|
265|“자, 이제 초대받지 않은 놈들은 모두 꺼져라. 배고프면 밥이나 한 그릇 하고 가든가.”
266|
267|이제는 숫제 거지 취급이다. 모멸감에 몸을 떨던 노호검객이 한참 만에 입을 뗐다.
268|
269|“……그럼 이만 물러가겠습니다.”
270|
271|“멀리 안 나간다.”
272|
273|“가자!”
274|
275|노호검객은 그 말을 기다렸다는 듯 세차게 돌아섰다. 오만상을 쓰고 있던 공일혁과 종남삼수의 두 사람이 그 뒤를 따랐다.
276|
277|네 사람의 등 뒤를 따가운 시선들이 쫓았다. 대문을 나서려던 그가 문득 고개를 돌려 나를 응시했다.
278|
279|살기가 담긴 한 줄기 전음과 함께.
280|
281|- 저 늙은이와 무슨 인연이 있는지는 모르겠으나…… 내 숨이 붙어 있는 한 반드시 네놈과 태원진가를 벌할 것이다.
282|
283|그건 찰나라고 부를 수 있을 만큼 짧은 순간 벌어진 일이었다.
284|
285|이내 어둠 속으로 녹아드는 노호검객의 뒷모습을 알 수 없는 표정으로 바라보던 화왕이 한 마디를 툭 던졌다.
286|
287|“잠시 나갔다 오마.”
288|
289|“예? 어디 가시게요?”
290|
291|“이 나이에 소피보러 가는 것도 일일이 보고하리?”
292|
293|퉁명스럽게 내뱉은 그는 팔자걸음으로 사라졌다.
294|
295|
296|
297|* * *
298|

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fence or prose:

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fence or prose:

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 193

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃193화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|열화문의 신물.
  6|
  7|화왕의 입에서 그 낯선 단어가 튀어나온 순간, 노호검객의 눈이 찢어질 듯 팽창했다.
  8|
  9|“그, 그게 무슨 말씀이십니까.”
 10|
 11|“칠순도 안 된 놈이 벌써부터 귓구멍이 막혔나. 한 번 더 말해 줄 테니 똑똑히 들어라.”
 12|
 13|적천강이 짜증 난 듯한 얼굴로 나를 향해 턱짓했다.
 14|
 15|“본문의 신물을 저놈한테 맡겼다. 됐느냐?”
 16|
 17|“…….”
 18|
 19|“…….”
 20|
 21|되긴 뭐가 돼.
 22|
 23|나는 황당한 얼굴로 주위를 둘러봤다. 진위경과 백무성을 포함한 모두가 경악한 얼굴로 나와 적천강을 번갈아 보는 중이었다.
 24|
 25|이 혼돈의 도가니 속, 유일하게 영향을 받지 않은 한 사람이 입을 열었다.
 26|
 27|“은인, 열화문의 신물이 뭐예요? 나도 보여 줘요.”
 28|
 29|나는 청풍의 질문에 대답할 수 없었다.
 30|
 31|‘나도 몰라, 이 새끼야.’
 32|
 33|열화문의 신물이라니. 뭐야 그게.
 34|
 35|맹세컨대 그런 물건은 듣도 보도 못했다.
 36|
 37|내가 적천강에게 받은 물건이라고는 화염신장의 비급과 검 한 자루뿐인……데.
 38|
 39|아, 잠깐만.
 40|
 41|“혹시?”
 42|
 43|설마 하는 내 시선에 적천강이 혀를 찼다.
 44|
 45|“등에 메어 놓고도 모르다니. 멍청한 놈.”
 46|
 47|망치로 뒤통수를 얻어맞은 기분이다.
 48|
 49|나는 황급히 단단히 고정시킨 매듭을 풀었다. 칭칭 감싸 둔 천을 벗겨 내자 낡고 투박한 검갑이 모습을 드러낸다.
 50|
 51|‘이름 없는 검.’
 52|
 53|조필이 스승에게서 훔치고, 나에게 빼앗긴 바로 그 물건.
 54|
 55|검파를 움켜쥐고 당겼다.
 56|
 57|스르릉, 솜털이 곤두서는 소리와 함께 새하얀 검신이 드러난다.
 58|
 59|내리깔린 어둠 속, 마치 전설 속 성검(聖劍)처럼 빛나는 모습에 사람들이 탄성을 내질렀다.
 60|
 61|‘그럼 이게 정말…… 열화문의 신물?’
 62|
 63|지금까지 단 한 번도 의심해 보지 않았다.
 64|
 65|왜 조필이 적천강에게서 이것을 훔쳤는지. 왜 화염신장이나 열화신단과 달리 [이름 없는 검]이라는 괴상한 설명이 붙었는지.
 66|
 67|내가 넋 나간 얼굴로 검신을 바라보던 그때였다.
 68|
 69|“이, 이건 말도 안 됩니다!”
 70|
 71|노호검객이다. 극도의 당황과 흥분에 휩싸인 그와는 달리 적천강의 안색은 평온, 그 자체였다.
 72|
 73|“무엇이 말이냐?”
 74|
 75|“그, 그것이.”
 76|
 77|“노부가 저 녀석에게 열화문의 신물을 맡겼다. 네놈이 제아무리 대가리에 똥만 가득 찬 놈이라지만 그것이 무슨 뜻인지 모르지 않을 터.”
 78|
 79|순간 정신이 번쩍 들었다.
 80|
 81|검에 정신이 팔려서 잠시 잊고 있었다. 한 문파, 그것도 수백 년간 일인전승으로 계승된 열화문의 신물이 가진 의미를.
 82|
 83|더불어 불과 반나절 전에 청풍이 했던 말이 뇌리를 스쳤다.
 84|
 85|
 86|
 87|‘은인을 제자로 삼으려는 것 아니에요?’
 88|
 89|
 90|
 91|당시에는 허무맹랑한 헛소리라 생각하고 웃어넘겼다.
 92|
 93|하지만 이제는…….
 94|
 95|‘시바, 나도 모르겠다.’
 96|
 97|마른침만 꼴깍거리는 내게 노호검객의 삿대질이 날아들었다.
 98|
 99|하지만 미처 입을 떼기도 전에 적천강의 무시무시한 눈빛이 그를 꽁꽁 옭아맸다.
100|
101|“노부가, 본문의 신물을, 맡겼다고 했다.”
102|
103|그것이 전부였다. 하지만 상대는 다름 아닌 화왕이다.
104|
105|노호검객에게는 반박할 수 있는 용기가 남아 있지 않았다. 입술을 잘근잘근 씹던 그가 돌연 나를 노려보았다.
106|
107|“놈. 운이 좋구나.”
108|
109|이 노인네는 왜 또 나한테 지랄이야.
110|
111|적천강도 별말이 없다. 이 정도는 알아서 해결하라는 건가? 나는 노호검객을 향해 어깨를 으쓱해 보였다.

I had been so absorbed in the sword that I had momentarily forgotten what it meant for a sect’s sacred treasure to be entrusted to someone—especially the treasure of the Fire Gate Clan, whose lineage had been passed from one person to the next for hundreds of years.

[P42]
At the same time, Cheongpung’s words from barely half a day ago flashed through my mind.

[P43]
*“Aren’t you trying to take Benefactor as your Disciple?”*

[P44]
At the time, I had dismissed it as ridiculous nonsense and laughed it off.

[P45]
But now…

[P46]
*Fuck. I have no idea.*

[P47]
As I swallowed dryly, the Roaring Fury Swordsman thrust a finger at me.

[P48]
Before he could speak, however, Jeok Cheongang’s terrifying gaze locked him in place.

[P49]
“This old man said he entrusted our sect’s sacred treasure to him.”

[P50]
That was all.

[P51]
But the man speaking was none other than the Fire King.

[P52]
The Roaring Fury Swordsman had no courage left to argue. He chewed on his lip, then suddenly glared at me.

[P53]
“You bastard. You’re lucky.”

[P54]
*Why is this old man starting shit with me again?*

[P55]
Jeok Cheongang said nothing. Did he expect me to handle this much on my own?

[P56]
I shrugged at the Roaring Fury Swordsman.

[P57]
“You’ve got the wrong man. I’m actually really unlucky.”

[P58]
*If I were fucking lucky, would I have met a piece of shit like you?*

[P59]
The situation had been a hair’s breadth from exploding when Jeok Cheongang appeared, so I wasn’t sure whether to call it great misfortune or great fortune.

[P60]
“Anyway, it was nice meeting you. Have a safe trip home.”

[P61]
“You cunning bastard. Why don’t you try what you did earlier?”

[P62]
“What I did earlier? Oh, you mean when I said it was fucking bullshit?”

[P63]
Before the Roaring Fury Swordsman could respond, I bowed my head.

[P64]
“I apologize for that. I’ve never been able to tolerate injustice. Please forgive a slip of the tongue from a junior far beneath you. Great. Hero.”

[P65]
“…!”

[P66]
The Roaring Fury Swordsman trembled. Blood dripped from his tightly clenched fists.

[P67]
Looking at him, I saw myself from only a few minutes earlier. The difference between us was that I had refused to submit to the Roaring Fury Swordsman, while he had submitted to the Fire King.

[P68]
Those who wielded power knelt before even greater power. Being reminded of that fundamental truth of the world wasn’t entirely satisfying.

[P69]
If anything, it left me bitter.

[P70]
*This leaves a bad taste in my mouth.*

[P71]
If Jeok Cheongang hadn’t been here, the humiliation and fury that man now felt would have belonged to me and the Jin Family of Taiyuan.

[P72]
If a few of the people here joined forces, defeating the Roaring Fury Swordsman himself wouldn’t be difficult. But the Zhongnan Sect stood behind him.

[P73]
I hated admitting it, but the gap between us and them was vast. For now, it was a gap we could never bridge.

[P74]
*For now.*

[P75]
I had been a perpetual F-rank Hunter, yet I had still made it this far. No one knew what the future held.

[P76]
Maybe one day, the Jin Family of Taiyuan would stand shoulder to shoulder with the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families.

[P77]
*Okay, am I getting a little ahead of myself?*

[P78]
It was like the head of some rural township running for President.

[P79]
I let out a quiet laugh at the thought, and the Roaring Fury Swordsman ground his teeth.

[P80]
“How dare you laugh at me?”

[P81]
“My face just naturally looks like it’s smiling.”

[P82]
“Shut that mouth of yours!”

[P83]
The instant his furious shout rang out, Jeok Cheongang’s right foot shot forward like lightning and slammed into the Roaring Fury Swordsman’s shin.

[P84]
A shin kick from a Supreme Peak master.

[P85]
*Thud!*

[P86]
“Guh!”

[P87]
“You shut up. How dare a young bastard like you raise his voice in front of an elder?”

[P88]
“What do you think you’re doing?”

[P89]
“Look at this bastard. I tried to end things nicely, and now you’re asking for a beating?”

[P90]
*Wham!*

[P91]
“Urgh!”

[P92]
*Wow. That one really landed.*

[P93]
With an even duller impact than before, the Roaring Fury Swordsman clutched his shin and collapsed.

[P94]
*Even an Elder of the Great Zhongnan Sect is helpless against him.*

[P95]
The man was over sixty and held a lofty position, but his opponent was simply beyond comparison.

[P96]
Age, martial arts, status—there was no catching up to the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, in any of them.

[P97]
“Carrying on like that is a disease. You’ve done enough, so get the hell out of here.”

[P98]
“…Very well.”

[P99]
The Roaring Fury Swordsman glared resentfully at me as he rose, his body covered in dirt. Then Jeok Cheongang’s cold voice followed.

[P100]
“And I will let today’s events pass, so you will never speak of this matter again. Do you understand?”

[P101]
*I really should start a fan club.*

[P102]
I had acted on impulse, but the truth was, I had been worried. If the Roaring Fury Swordsman later used the Zhongnan Sect to retaliate, the Jin Family of Taiyuan would have no way to stop him.

[P103]
But with Jeok Cheongang mediating, that changed everything.

[P104]
*Though I’m not sure whether to call this mediation or a threat.*

[P105]
Resentment over what had happened today would remain, but at least he wouldn’t be able to bring official pressure against us.

[P106]
Even if he did, having the Fire King as a sturdy shield took a great deal of the pressure off.

[P107]
“Why aren’t you answering?”

[P108]
The Roaring Fury Swordsman’s face twisted horribly now that his little scheme had been seen through. Jeok Cheongang, of course, couldn’t have cared less.

[P109]
“Say it yourself. Right now.”

[P110]
“…Understood. I swear it on my name.”

[P111]
“What name do you have worth staking? Swear it in the name of the Zhongnan Sect.”

[P112]
“Grrk… Understood.”

[P113]
Only then did a satisfied smile appear on Jeok Cheongang’s lips. He chuckled and patted the Roaring Fury Swordsman on the shoulder.

[P114]
“Where did a young bastard like you learn to grind his teeth like that? Maybe I should yank out every last one of them.”

[P115]
“…”

[P116]
“Hohoho! But this old man is getting on in years. I couldn’t possibly do such a thing in front of all these people. Hahahaha!”

[P117]
I had never known that the laughter of a snow-white-haired old man could be so terrifying.

[P118]
Not only the Roaring Fury Swordsman, but everyone listening flinched at once.

[P119]
Jeok Cheongang, who had been laughing like a fiend, turned to me.

[P120]
“You’re not blameless either. Whatever the circumstances, how could you hurl such abuse at an elder so far above you in age? Are you out of your mind?”

[P121]
I immediately bowed my head. Whatever else had happened, that much was true, and I also thought it was time to settle matters with the Roaring Fury Swordsman, an Elder of the Zhongnan Sect.

[P122]
“I’m sorry.”

[P123]
“Even if he shoved all those years up his ass, he’s over sixty. He’s old enough to have a grandchild your age.”

[P124]
“…Ah. Yes.”

[P125]
“No matter how much of a bastard he is, he’s still your elder and a great Senior of Murim. No matter how filthy and unfair it feels, you must show him the proper respect from now on.”

[P126]
“Great Hero Song, I sincerely apologize.”

[P127]
When I straightened from my deep bow, the Roaring Fury Swordsman’s face was flushed scarlet.

[P128]
Even after receiving an apology, he probably didn’t feel as though he had gotten one.

[P129]
Meanwhile, despite apologizing to someone I hated, I felt as refreshed as if I had just finished circulating my qi.

[P130]
*Is this what comes with age?*

[P131]
Just look at those verbal skills, honed over a hundred years.

[P132]
His martial arts weren’t the only thing at Supreme Peak. At this point, he could change his title from Fire King to Tongue King.

[P133]
Having personally overseen the entire settlement, the Tongue King declared in a stern voice,

[P134]
“All right. Now all the uninvited guests can get the hell out. If you’re hungry, have a bowl of rice before you go.”

[P135]
Now he was openly treating them like beggars.

[P136]
The Roaring Fury Swordsman trembled with humiliation. It was a long while before he finally spoke.

[P137]
“…Then we will take our leave.”

[P138]
“I won’t see you out.”

[P139]
“Let’s go!”

[P140]
As though he had been waiting for those words, the Roaring Fury Swordsman spun around. Gong Ilhyuk and the other two members of the Three Hands of Zhongnan, their faces twisted into ugly grimaces, followed him.

[P141]
Scorching gazes pursued the four men’s backs. Just before stepping through the main gate, the Roaring Fury Swordsman suddenly turned and stared at me.

[P142]
A thread of Sound Transmission filled with killing intent reached my ears.

[P143]
—*I don’t know what connection you have with that old man… but as long as I draw breath, I will punish you and the Jin Family of Taiyuan.*

[P144]
It all happened in the briefest of instants.

[P145]
The Fire King watched the Roaring Fury Swordsman’s back melt into the darkness, his expression unreadable. Then he tossed out a single remark.

[P146]
“I’ll step out for a while.”

[P147]
“Yes? Where are you going?”

[P148]
“At my age, do I need to report every time I go take a piss?”

[P149]
With that gruff reply, he disappeared with a bowlegged gait.

[P150]
* * *

[P151]
Once he was a good distance from the Jin Family of Taiyuan, the Roaring Fury Swordsman suddenly drew his sword and swung.

[P152]
*Whoooosh! Boom!*

[P153]
Dozens of streams of Sword Energy sliced through trees and shattered rocks. After venting his fury for quite some time, he finally turned it on the Three Hands of Zhongnan, Gong Ilhyuk included.

[P154]
“You damned idiots…”

[P155]
“E-Elder.”

[P156]
“Do you know what kind of humiliation this old man suffered because of you?”

[P157]
“I-I’m sorry. Please forgive your foolish Disciples.”

[P158]
The Three Hands of Zhongnan froze.

[P159]
Gong Ilhyuk was the most terrified of them all. If he hadn’t incited the Roaring Fury Swordsman to come to the Jin Family of Taiyuan, none of this would have happened.

[P160]
“E-Elder, please calm down and hear me out.”

[P161]
“I turned a blind eye a few times because you’re related by marriage to my Junior Brother, the Sect Leader, and now it seems you’ve forgotten your place.”

[P162]
*Clench!*

[P163]
The Roaring Fury Swordsman’s gaunt hand closed around Gong Ilhyuk’s throat.

[P164]
“Guh… I-I’m the Sect Leader’s…”

[P165]
“Do you think my Junior Brother, the Sect Leader, would so much as blink if this old man punished the likes of you? You worthless piece of trash.”

[P166]
Gong Ilhyuk’s face went deathly pale.

[P167]
Then—

[P168]
*Thump. Thump. Thud.*

[P169]
His body went limp, his head lolling to one side. The other two members of the Three Hands, who had been frozen with fear, also crumpled helplessly to the ground.

[P170]
“W-why did these bastards suddenly…”

[P171]
Momentarily confused, the Roaring Fury Swordsman turned his head. He stared into the darkness before speaking.

[P172]
“Do you still have business with me?”

[P173]
“Why else would I have come looking for you?”

[P174]
Along with that calm voice, a small old man emerged.

[P175]
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.

[P176]
He clicked his tongue as he looked at the fallen Three Hands of Zhongnan.

[P177]
“Tsk, tsk. Seems I ended up saving those bastards without meaning to. Maybe I should have come a little later.”

[P178]
“Why have you come back?”

[P179]
“It’s been so long. It seemed a shame to let you go just like that.”

[P180]
The Fire King smiled faintly and added,

[P181]
“There was also something I forgot.”

[P182]
“Something you forgot? What do you mean…”

[P183]
At that moment, Jeok Cheongang’s figure vanished like a phantom.

[P184]
At the same time, Sword Energy erupted from the Roaring Fury Swordsman’s waist.

[P185]
*Sh-sh-sh-sh-shk!*

[P186]
A dense net of Sword Energy spread across a three-jang radius, ready to slice through flesh and bone the instant anything touched it.

[P187]
But the big fish had already swum against the current and escaped the net.

[P188]
“I told you earlier. Don’t touch so much as a hair on that boy’s head.”

[P189]
*Crack!*

[P190]
The sword hilt dropped from the Roaring Fury Swordsman’s hand. His wrist broken, he screamed and drove his knee upward.

[P191]
“Gyaaah! You fucking old bastard!”

[P192]
“When will you finally learn to act like a human being?”

[P193]
At the same instant, a palm shrouded in pure-white flame pressed against the Roaring Fury Swordsman’s chest.

[P194]
*Boom!*

[P195]
“Guh…!”

[P196]
An unavoidable palm strike.

[P197]
His Body-Protecting Qi shattered, and his flesh and bones seared. He vomited blood and sank to his knees, his eyelids trembling.

[P198]
“Cough… F-Flame Divine Palm…”

[P199]
“Raise your head and look at me.”

[P200]
The old man’s voice was so cold that it belied his title of Fire King.

[P201]
The Roaring Fury Swordsman barely managed to lift his head and found himself staring into a pair of eyes where blue ghostly flames flickered.

[P202]
“F-Fire King.”

[P203]
“That’s right. This old man is the Fire King.”

[P204]
He had briefly forgotten just what kind of monster the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, truly was.

[P205]
Jeok Cheongang had spent only one year of his entire life active in Murim. Yet a single battle had made him a legend and carved his name into Murim history.

[P206]
He was an opponent the Roaring Fury Swordsman could never hope to resist.

[P207]
Deep despair settled over the Roaring Fury Swordsman’s face.

[P208]
“Are you… are you planning to kill me?”

[P209]
“If killing you could put an end to everything, this old man would have done it long ago.”

[P210]
“Then…”

[P211]
“Remember just one thing.”

[P212]
The Fire King slowly parted his lips.

[P213]
“You may kill Jin Taekyung. You may even wipe out the Jin Family of Taiyuan, and I will stand by and watch. But if that happens, I will go to the Zhongnan Sect.”

[P214]
“…!”

[P215]
“I will smash the Zhongnan Sect’s signboard and burn Mount Zhongnan. If you abandon your main sect and flee, I will hunt you down to the ends of the earth and kill every last one of you. Until the day I draw my final breath.”

[P216]
The Roaring Fury Swordsman’s entire body trembled beneath that terrifying killing intent.

[P217]
Jeok Cheongang meant every word. He was declaring that he would take on the Zhongnan Sect alone.

[P218]
If that ever happened, there was no telling how many lives would be lost.

[P219]
“W-what am I supposed to do?”

[P220]
“The choice is yours. The punishment that follows is mine.”

[P221]
Leaving only those words behind, Jeok Cheongang vanished without a trace.

[P222]
It was a long while before the Three Hands of Zhongnan finally awoke. They jolted in alarm when they found the Roaring Fury Swordsman sitting there in a daze.

[P223]
“E-Elder!”

[P224]
“What happened?”

[P225]
“Who in the world did this?”

[P226]
A very long time passed before the Roaring Fury Swordsman finally spoke.

[P227]
“We’re going back. To Zhongnan.”

[P228]
His voice was steeped in terror, and the Three Hands of Zhongnan could say nothing.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
